angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 77,606,726 km at 119.76 pc = 8.66 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 82273: distance 119.76 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.018), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 119.76 +/- 2.156 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 111.552 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 82273: radius 111.552 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 3713.19 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.061) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 77,606,726 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4269 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 82273: effective temperature 4269 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.065) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 82273: effective temperature 4269 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.065) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf TrA: spectral type K2III_Ba1 (1991AJ....101.2229L)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf TrA: main object type *, Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * alf TrA: projected rotation speed 6.4 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 0.92 from 2014AJ....147..137L; the 5 published values span log g 0.82 to 1.5, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.3% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014AJ....147..137L)
